subject: Acme Data Solutions — incentive matrix and migration economics
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmedata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@modelflow.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick ask — pricing match + onboarding economics

Hannah,

Hope you're well. We're coming up on renewal with ModelFlow and procurement pushed back saying Redwood's feature set looks good but the unit economics we're getting from ModelFlow are hard to justify. They gave us an aggressive blended rate that includes a migration credit and a 12-month usage commitment.

High-level: can Redwood present a price-match / replacement package that includes one-time migration credit and assistance for tenant onboarding? Our procurement team wants a simple incentives matrix to compare total cost of ownership over 12 and 24 months.

If you can share a short matrix (credits, term discounts, onboarding assistance, professional services hours) we can fast-track the SOW/PO review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Liam
Director of Engineering
Acme Data Solutions
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmedata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pricing match + onboarding economics

Liam —

Thanks for the note. Short answer: yes, we can put together a competitive replacement package. At a glance, the levers we typically use are:
- one-time onboarding / migration credit (applied to first invoice)
- committed-month discount ladder (12/24 month tiers)
- dedicated migration support hours (Redwood Solutions)
- optional dedicated capacity credit for first 3 months for burst coverage

I’ve looped in Rishi for the detailed matrix and numbers. To make the comparison apples-to-apples can you share the ModelFlow effective blended rate (tokens/embedding units + any fixed monthly fees) and the size of the committed term they're quoting? If you prefer, we can fill in the matrix with two scenarios: (A) match their blended unit economics and (B) 10% below for a 12-month commit.

We’ll also include an estimated migration timeline and a stub SOW for professional services so procurement can see deliverables and milestones.

Happy to set up a 30-min call tomorrow.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmedata.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pricing match + onboarding economics

Liam —

Appreciate the context. Attached is an initial Incentive Matrix and a quick migration cost comparison (attachment: migration-cost-comparison.xlsx). The matrix includes five common levers across three commitment profiles: 12m small, 12m enterprise, 24m enterprise. Highlights: 

- Migration credit: up to USD 60k applied over first two invoices for enterprise-sized migrations (we can flex this based on documented integration effort).
- Term discounts: 12m (5–12% tiered), 24m (10–18% tiered) dependent on committed usage bands.
- Onboarding hours: 40 complimentary hours for standard migrations; additional PS at blended rate.
- Dedicated capacity credit: first 3 months waiver for reserved capacity fees for customers that sign a 12m+ reserved plan.

I also attached a draft term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-ACME-2026-08.pdf) with standard ELAs, termination, and data isolation language. If procurement needs tighter language around audit logs and retention, Laura can help scope SOC2 artifacts.

Next steps I recommend:
1) You confirm the ModelFlow blended rate and exact committed TU (tokens/month or embedding units).
2) We formalize the two favored scenarios (match vs aggressive) and produce a short SOW + timeline.
3) If acceptable, we push to an expedited procurement review with a 1-week turnaround target for PO.

Attachments:
- migration-cost-comparison.xlsx (attachment stub)
- redwood-term-sheet-ACME-2026-08.pdf (attachment stub)

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmedata.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pricing match + onboarding economics

Thanks Rishi — the matrix is helpful. A couple clarifications from procurement:
- ModelFlow offered a ~15% blended discount plus a USD 45k migration credit and 60 hours of migration assistance; they also included a 90-day dedicated capacity credit.
- The main procurement ask is an explicit line item showing the net first-year cost (including credits + waived fees) and an estimate of migration effort that we can attach to the PO.

If you can add a scenario that replicates ModelFlow (we'll call it Scenario M) and an alternative (Scenario R) where Redwood sits 8–12% below their blended rate on a 12-month commit, that will let us present both to leadership. Also curious whether the migration credit would be invoiced as a credit or applied as a price adjustment on the first invoice (procurement prefers credit line on invoice).

We could do a short call Friday morning to run through the numbers.

— Liam
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmedata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pricing match + onboarding economics

Liam —

Understood. We’ll produce: Scenario M (ModelFlow parity) and Scenario R (Redwood aggressive at ~10% below blended rate) with a single-line net-first-year figure (credits + waived fees), and explicit invoice language stating the migration credit will appear as an invoice credit applied to invoice #1 and documented on the SOW.

I’ve added Laura to scope SOC2 evidence and retention clauses if procurement raises questions. Rishi will update the matrix and push revised attachments to the shared Drive folder and HubSpot deal record by EOD Thursday.

Meeting: I booked a 30-min slot Friday 09:30–10:00 ET — link: https://hubspot.example.com/meetings/83421. If that doesn't work reply with a time and we’ll adjust.

Next deliverables (by EOD Thu):
- Revised incentive matrix with Scenario M + Scenario R (attachment: migration-cost-comparison.xlsx v2)
- Short SOW outline and draft term-sheet v2 (attachment: redwood-term-sheet-ACME-2026-08-v2.pdf)
- HubSpot deal link and DocuSign stub for expedited approval.

Hannah Schmitt
